items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: The man who published my first book called, 'You Don't Look Like a Musician,' a book of anecdotes and vignettes, is a black biochemist

ctx.x: Yes, there were many, many superior players who were white. Today you've got some of the finest drummers -- Buddy Rich. What's the chap's name who is married to -- Louis Bellson, people like this, there's so many great -- now I think and here is a very interesting thing -- I want to make sure not to get off the track here.

The man who published my first book called, 'You Don't Look Like a Musician,' a book of anecdotes and vignettes, is a black biochemist, a brilliant man, a genius at Fort Wayne University, yes, in Detroit -- is it Fort Wayne University -- Wayne State, beg your pardon. I am sorry. I was thinking about something about Fort Wayne. I want to tell you later.

But I mean of course Wayne State University and he again is a black man, a great biochemist and he asked if he could read the manuscript of my first book. Now, in the first book I tell this very story, I praise the black people and I explain -- I even go so far as to suggest the music might have come from Africa, well, this man, this black biochemist, Professor James, said no, I do not agree that jazz came from Africa.
